meta.title: Glens Falls trees from USGS 3DEP airborne LiDAR (canopy tops)
meta.dataset: USGS 3DEP NY_Hudson_D22, work unit NY_Hudson_1_D22 (QL2; Sanborn, Riegl VQ-1560 II)
meta.classification: The point cloud has no vegetation (3/4/5) or building (6) class: 1 unclassified, 2 ground, 7/18 noise, 9 water, 17 bridge deck, 20 ignored ground. Vegetation is therefore inferred (see method).
meta.licence: USGS 3DEP data are U.S. Government works in the public domain; credit requested
meta.credit: Tree positions and heights: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP), NY_Hudson_D22 LiDAR, 2022-23. Masks: © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL 1.0) and Overture Maps buildings 2026-10-21.0
meta.method: Class-1 points 2-50 m above the USGS 1 m bare-earth DEM (bilinear), minus points on any building footprint (GF_BUILDINGS at d6d693c + Overture buildings, each grown 1 m), make a 1 m canopy height model (highest return per cell). It is smoothed (Gaussian sigma 1.2 m) only to find peaks: a top is a cell that is the maximum of its 7 x 7 m window and at least 2.5 m high. Tops closer than r(h) = clamp(1 + 0.12 h, 2, 5) m to a taller top are dropped as the same crown. height_m = highest real return within ~1.5 m of the peak above the DEM. crown_r_m = equal-area radius of the canopy cells (>= 2 m and >= 40% of the top) nearest to this top within 9 m. Each top then gets one flag (first rule that applies, in rules.order). 4 x 4 tiles with ~60-80 m overlap; each top is written by the one tile whose core holds it.
meta.notSpecies: LiDAR gives position, height and spread only. No species, age or condition is measured or implied.
meta.notHistoric: Trees as flown Nov 2022 - Apr 2023, not 1993. Trees planted, grown or removed since 1993 are not corrected.
meta.leafOffCaveat: Flown leaf-off: deciduous crowns return only branches, so small or thin trees are missed and some crowns split into two tops; evergreens return fully. Counts are an estimate of canopy tops, not a tree census.

flags.ok: used: a canopy top that passes every check below
flags.water: not used: the top is over a GF_GEO water polygon (river, pond, canal): overhanging bank trees or bridge/dam parts
flags.in-road: not used: the top is closer than half the curb width + 0.5 m to a GF_GEO road centreline (exact vector test), i.e. a trunk there would stand in or touch the carriageway. Mostly real street trees whose crown peak overhangs the road; kept out so no trunk stands in a lane. Not moved, not replaced
flags.near-wall: not used: the top is within 1 m of a GF_BUILDINGS footprint (exact vector test): a trunk there would touch the wall
flags.building-edge: not used: within 3 m of a building footprint (GF_BUILDINGS or Overture), at that building's own roof height (roof p50 - 2 m .. roof p98 + 1.5 m) and fewer than 80% multi-return points: an eave, wall or roof edge the footprint does not cover
flags.tall: not used: higher than 40 m (towers, stacks, tall roofs; no tree in the area is expected that tall)
flags.low: not used: highest return under 3 m above ground (shrub, fence, vehicle, sign)
flags.sparse: not used: fewer than 8 vegetation points within 2 m of the top in its upper half
flags.linear: not used: the points round the top lie on a near-horizontal line (PCA linearity > 0.92 and the main axis's vertical component < 0.5, i.e. under 30 degrees from level): overhead wires or a cable. Vertical lines are kept: they are conifer leaders and bare deciduous tops
flags.small: not used: canopy spread under 1.5 m equal-area radius: usually a utility pole with wires
flags.structure: not used: fewer than 20% of the points round the top are multi-return (leaf-off tree crowns are ~90% multi-return, roofs ~23%): most likely an unmapped roof, tank or other solid structure
